findings.summary: Sparse Structures globally doubles spacing for all structure placements; mansion receives an additional factor of 2.
Structure Essentials also owns a global spacing/separation modifier, but its effective value is neutral (1.0).

YUNG's generated defaults disable six vanilla structure sets; IDAS also disables vanilla desert pyramids and Integrated Villages disables vanilla villages. Desert-pyramid replacement is therefore controlled by both YUNG and IDAS.
C2ME records that its End biome cache optimization is disabled at runtime because Biolith 3.0.10 is incompatible.
Village generation is controlled by multiple providers and pool injectors; actual registry/datapack precedence requires Item 7 runtime inspection.

Better Dungeons exposes top-level gameplay controls and separate Cristel Lib placement and toggle controls. The audit records both layers without claiming runtime precedence. Sparse Structures can also multiply the enabled placement spacing.

YUNG's API, YUNG's Bridges, and YUNG's Extras generated no standalone config surface. Better Caves generated documentation and liquid-region data, YUNG's Better End Island generated End platform and gateway gameplay options, and YUNG's Cave Biomes generated biome, noise, and weather controls. Those retained surfaces are present but do not define the Item 6 structure placement or replacement controls audited above.

limitations: Generated files do not expose every loader or datapack implicit default; absence is recorded rather than guessed.
The effective multiplicative composition of Sparse Structures with provider spacing is an implementation inference to verify empirically in Items 7 and 10.
No Item 7 terrain observation or Item 8 family inventory is claimed by this audit.
